compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/_config_sources.py` is **791 LOC** on origin/main @ e278425d7a (re-measured after
today's six sibling splits; the figure is unchanged from 059d54b725). That is nine lines under
the locked 800-LOC cap in `.github/module-size-limit.txt` and inside the gate's `>= 720`
near-cap warning band. It is the last unowned file in that band, so the next config change to
land breaks CI.

## Approach
Split at the **concern boundary the source already draws in-file**: the raw-input resolution
layer versus the RP-04 below-seam *owned resolvers*.

- **Stays in `_config_sources.py` — raw-input resolution (lines 31-361).** Repo-root and
  config-file location (`repo_root`, `config_file`, `tracker_dir_override`), the mtime-keyed
  TOML parse cache (`_TOML_CACHE`, `_parse_toml`, `_read_toml_table`, `_pyproject_rebar_state`),
  project/user config discovery (`_discover_project_config`, `user_config_path`), the deep merge
  (`_deep_merge`), the LLM-config-file pointer (`llm_config_file_pointer`,
  `layer_llm_config_file`), and the `REBAR_<SECTION>_<KEY>` env-override layer
  (`_CANONICAL_ENV_NAMES`, `_canonical_env_name`, `_LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES`, `_map_legacy_env`,
  `env_overrides`, `_strict_unknown_keys`). This is exactly what the module docstring at
  `src/rebar/_config_sources.py:1-15` already describes, and exactly what `load_config` consumes.
- **Moves to a new `src/rebar/_config_resolvers.py` — the RP-04 owned resolvers (lines 364-791).**
  The three banner-delimited blocks the source itself labels "Below-seam config resolvers"
  (`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:364-374`, ticket d074), "Below-seam CLI/command resolvers"
  (`:514-523`, ticket 9515) and "Below-seam LLM-subsystem resolvers" (`:589-601`, ticket 1b07),
  plus the "Reconciler JIRA-family resolvers" block (`:685-690`). These are the 24 `resolve_*`
  entry points plus their four private helpers (`_positive_int`, `_snapshot_table`,
  `_snapshot_int`, `_gate_str_pref`) and the constant `_DEFAULT_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE`.

**Why the call graph supports it.** The dependency is strictly one-directional and narrow: no
symbol in the raw-input half names any resolver, and exactly **one** resolver body
(`_snapshot_table`, `src/rebar/_config_sources.py:440-458`) reaches back into the raw-input half
— for `user_config_path`, `_read_toml_table` and `_discover_project_config`. Everything else in
the moving half touches only stdlib (`os`, `subprocess`, `pathlib.Path`,
`collections.abc.Mapping`) or, in the reconciler family, `rebar.config` through an already-lazy
in-body `import rebar.config as _cfg`. Neither `ConfigError`, `_as_bool`, `_SECTIONS`,
`warn_deprecated` nor `logger` is used by the moving half, so the new module is a stdlib-only
leaf with the same no-`rebar.config`-import invariant.

**Binding preservation (the Gerrit 1932 regression class).** In `_snapshot_table` the three
raw-input names are resolved through a **lazy in-body** `from rebar import _config_sources` and
called as attributes at call time. Attribute lookup on the module object hits the same
`_config_sources.__dict__` slot the current module-global lookup hits, so late binding is
byte-identical to today and any present or future `monkeypatch.setattr(_config_sources, ...)`
keeps applying. It also keeps the module pair acyclic: `_config_sources.py` re-exports the
resolvers with a top-level `from rebar._config_resolvers import X as X` block, and
`_config_resolvers.py` has **no** top-level `rebar` import at all.

**Import surface.** `_config_sources.py` re-exports all 29 moved names (`X as X`, matching the
existing re-export idiom in `src/rebar/config.py:46-89`), so `rebar._config_sources.<name>` and
`rebar.config.<name>` keep resolving unchanged. `src/rebar/config.py` is untouched.

**Config-ownership seam.** No config read crosses the seam: the new module is the *same*
composition root, split in two. `scripts/check_config_ownership.py:46-53` classifies composition
roots by module **basename**, so `_config_resolvers.py` is added to `COMPOSITION_ROOT_BASENAMES`
alongside the `_config_sources.py` entry it inherits from. The env-name string literals stay
verbatim in the moved bodies, so `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` still sees them.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_config_sources.py` — remove lines 364-791; add the re-export block; update the
  module docstring to name the sibling.
- `src/rebar/_config_resolvers.py` — **new**; the moved resolvers.
- `scripts/check_config_ownership.py` — add `_config_resolvers.py` to
  `COMPOSITION_ROOT_BASENAMES`.
- `docs/env-vars.md` — **regenerate** with `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py`. It is
  CI-drift-gated by `.github/actions/docs-gates/action.yml:37-49` and records the owning file for
  every env name plus a `<file>:<line>` citation for non-literal reads; `docs/env-vars.md:181`
  currently cites `src/rebar/_config_sources.py:612` (`_gate_str_pref`), which this move
  relocates. Do not hand-edit.
- `tests/unit/test_config_resolver_seam.py` — **new** seam test file. No existing test file is
  modified.

## Testing
New file `tests/unit/test_config_resolver_seam.py`:
- **Happy path** — every moved name still resolves through `rebar._config_sources` *and*
  `rebar.config` (asserted against an explicit name list), and `rebar._config_resolvers` imports
  standalone.
- **Binding / regression path** — `monkeypatch.setattr(_config_sources, "_discover_project_config", ...)`
  and `..., "user_config_path", ...` still steer `_config_resolvers._snapshot_table`, proving the
  late binding the move could have broken. Confirmed RED first by binding the names eagerly.
- **Edge path** — `_config_resolvers` has no module-level `rebar` import (acyclic leaf), asserted
  by AST over its source; and `_config_resolvers.py` is a recognised composition root under
  `scripts/check_config_ownership.py`, so an env read in it does not fire the ownership gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `wc -l src/rebar/_config_sources.py` and `src/rebar/_config_resolvers.py` both report
      >= 100 and <= 500 LOC, leaving real headroom under the 800 cap.
- [x] The commit message names the concern boundary (raw-input resolution vs RP-04 below-seam
      owned resolvers) and cites the in-file banners that already draw it.
- [x] `sorted(dir(rebar._config_sources))` and `sorted(dir(rebar.config))` are supersets of the
      pre-split values captured from `origin/main`, so no previously-resolvable symbol is lost.
- [x] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`,
      and `git diff --exit-code -- .github/module-size-limit.txt .github/complexity-baseline.json`
      is clean.
- [x] `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py && git diff --exit-code -- docs/env-vars.md` is clean
      (regenerated in this change), and `python scripts/check_config_ownership.py` exits 0.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass, and the whole test tree (`tests/`, excluding
      `tests/external`) passes with **zero existing test files modified**
      (`git diff --stat` shows only the new test file under `tests/`).
